Ben / team — quick read of Acme's redlines and initial guidance. I added inline comments to the attached document and summarized below.

Summary of our position (short):
- Subprocessor notice: we should avoid unconditional 15-day approval windows. Proposed compromise = 14-day notice for material new subprocessors plus quarterly published subprocessor list; right to object limited to processors that handle account data or perform critical security functions. This is defensible and maps to our operational capability.
- Transfers: our standard approach is to rely on SCCs (we are processor under Acme as controller) plus a processor-to-controller attestation where necessary. We should not accept language that converts our role to a co-controller or that imposes additional transfer obligations beyond SCCs. If Acme insists on an 'EU-US Addendum' label, we can provide equivalent wording but prefer SCCs.
- Logs/retention: confirm that audit logs are pseudonymized and retained for up to 90 days for operational debugging; longer retention is possible with a business justification and customer request. Provide exact column list from ops (see Subprocessor_List file for context).

Recommended redlines (for countersign):
1) Accept notice window compromise (14 days) + quarterly list + ad-hoc notification upon changes; include explicit right to object limited to critical subprocessors with narrow definition.
2) Keep SCCs as primary transfer mechanism; add short paragraph explaining our standard SCC execution flow.
3) Confirm logs retention window and propose a sentence restricting export of customer-identifying fields without explicit request.

I attached a short DocuSign execution proposal (DocuSign_Exec_Proposal.pdf) that covers envelope owner and who signs first. If Ben/Monica agree to the compromise language I can produce a clean countersign version and route via DocuSign.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Redline_20280312.docx (with comments), DocuSign_Exec_Proposal.pdf
